preconditions.description: The first line of input is an integer t (1 ≤ t ≤ 10^4) representing the number of test cases.

preconditions.expression: all(line.strip() == '' for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:2*t] if line.strip() != '')
preconditions.description: Each test case is preceded by an empty line (except possibly the first line).

preconditions.expression: all(len(lines) == n + 1 for lines in [stdin.splitlines()[i:i+n+1] for i in range(2*t, len(stdin.splitlines()), n+2)])
preconditions.description: Each test case consists of n+1 lines: the first line contains n and k, followed by n-1 lines of edges.

preconditions.expression: all(all(u == int(u) and v == int(v) and 1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n and u != v for u, v in [line.split() for line in lines[1:]]) for lines in [stdin.splitlines()[i:i+n+1] for i in range(2*t, len(stdin.splitlines()), n+2)])
preconditions.description: Each edge is a pair of integers u and v (1 ≤ u, v ≤ n, u ≠ v) representing vertices connected by an edge.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= n <= 4*10**5 and 1 <= k <= 2*10**5 for n, k in [tuple(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdin.splitlines()[2*t::n+2]])
preconditions.description: For each test case, n (1 ≤ n ≤ 4*10^5) is the number of vertices, and k (1 ≤ k ≤ 2*10^5) is the number of operations.
The sum of n across all test cases does not exceed 4*10^5.

postconditions.description: The output contains exactly t lines, one for each test case.

postconditions.expression: all(output_line == str(int(output_line)) for output_line in stdout.splitlines())
postconditions.description: Each output line is a single integer representing the number of vertices remaining after k operations.

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= int(output_line) <= n for output_line, n in zip(stdout.splitlines(), [int(line.split()[0]) for line in stdin.splitlines()[2*t::n+2]]))
postconditions.description: The output integer for each test case is between 0 and n (inclusive), representing the remaining vertices after k operations.

postconditions.expression: all(remaining_vertices == 0 if k >= max_operations else remaining_vertices == n - k * leaves_removed for remaining_vertices, n, k, max_operations, leaves_removed in zip([int(line) for line in stdout.splitlines()], [int(line.split()[0]) for line in stdin.splitlines()[2*t::n+2]], [int(line.split()[1]) for line in stdin.splitlines()[2*t::n+2]], [max_operations_for_tree(n, edges) for n, edges in zip([int(line.split()[0]) for line in stdin.splitlines()[2*t::n+2]], [stdin.splitlines()[i+1:i+n] for i in range(2*t, len(stdin.splitlines()), n+2)])], [leaves_removed_per_operation(n, edges) for n, edges in zip([int(line.split()[0]) for line in stdin.splitlines()[2*t::n+2]], [stdin.splitlines()[i+1:i+n] for i in range(2*t, len(stdin.splitlines()), n+2)])]))
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output is 0 if k ≥ max_operations (the number of operations needed to remove all vertices), otherwise it is n - k * leaves_removed_per_operation, where leaves_removed_per_operation is the number of leaves removed in each operation (which is constant until the tree is reduced to 0 or 1 vertex).

postconditions.expression: all(remaining_vertices == 0 if n == 1 and k >= 1 else remaining_vertices == 0 if n == 2 and k >= 1 else remaining_vertices == max(0, n - k) if n <= 2 else remaining_vertices == max(0, n - k * leaves_removed_per_operation) for remaining_vertices, n, k, leaves_removed_per_operation in zip([int(line) for line in stdout.splitlines()], [int(line.split()[0]) for line in stdin.splitlines()[2*t::n+2]], [int(line.split()[1]) for line in stdin.splitlines()[2*t::n+2]], [leaves_removed_per_operation(n, edges) for n, edges in zip([int(line.split()[0]) for line in stdin.splitlines()[2*t::n+2]], [stdin.splitlines()[i+1:i+n] for i in range(2*t, len(stdin.splitlines()), n+2)])]))
postconditions.description: For special cases: if n=1 and k≥1, or n=2 and k≥1, the result is 0. Otherwise, the result is max(0, n - k * leaves_removed_per_operation), where leaves_removed_per_operation is the number of leaves removed in each operation (constant until the tree is reduced to 0 or 1 vertex).
